questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

The reason Priya was late (1)/ to the meeting is because her (2)/ flight was delayed. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** 2 

As the sentence already uses ‘the reason’, using ‘because’ in Sentence 2 is redundant. The correct sentence is: ‘The reason Priya was late to the meeting is that her flight was delayed.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Not only did they offer him (1)/ good salary but provided (2)/ him with a beautiful bungalow. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** 2 

‘Not only’ is always followed by ‘but also’, which is not the case in Sentence 2. The correct sentence is: ‘Not only did they offer him good salary but also provided him with a beautiful bungalow’.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

Neha (would be looked) beautiful in Indian attire.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: would look 

‘Would look’ indicates a future possibility of something happening, which fits the context of the sentence of ‘looking beautiful’. The other options make the sentence grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

(People have been long known) how important the trees are to them.
questions.solution:
The correct option is (3) People have long known.

The original sentence is in the present perfect tense, which is appropriate for the idea being conveyed. The phrase "long known" indicates that this knowledge has been held for a considerable amount of time, which makes sense in the context of the importance of trees to people.

Option (1) "People have to know long" is grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended meaning.

Option (2) "People had long known" uses the past perfect tense, which implies that the knowledge is no longer current. However, the original sentence indicates that the knowledge is still relevant.

Therefore, the best option is (3) "People have long known." This phrasing is grammatically correct and conveys the idea that people have possessed knowledge of the importance of trees for an extended period of time, which remains true in the present.

Option (4) "No improvement" is incorrect, as the sentence can be improved by selecting option (3).

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P- On the earth, liquid forms and solid forms (ice/snow) predominate. 

Q- The water cycle has two distinct branches the atmospheric branch and the terrestrial branch. 

R- Water plays a versatile role in the functioning of the biosphere. 

S- In the atmospheric, water exists mainly in gaseous form.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** RQSP

Sentence Q talks about the atmospheric branch first and then terrestrial branch. Therefore, the sentences following it should also be in the same order, i.e., S and then P. The correct order is RQSP.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

 P- For however elusively, it still knew of harbours and anchors, of homes to which to return, and of barns in which to store the harvest.

Q- The works of the early Renaissance and the poetry of Shakespeare vibrate with the compassion for live experience in danger of dying from exposure and neglect. 

R- Yes, it was a genius of courage, not of desperate audacity. 

S- In this compassion was the creative genius of the age.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: QSRP

From the sentences, it is clear that Sentence S is preceded by Sentence Q, since Q talks about compassion and S references it using ‘this’. Therefore, QS is a combination, which exists only in Option 3. Hence, the correct answer is QSRP.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Sunita has written a story which fascinates everyone.

options.text: A story which has been written by Sunita fascinates every one.
Everyone is fascinated by the story which has been written by Sunita.
Every one fascinates the story which is written by Sunita.
Story written by Sunita fascinates everyone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **active voice** and needs to be converted to the passive voice.
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence (a story) becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The **original action done by Sunita** (writing the story) is now being described as an action that the story (now the subject) has undergone by Sunita.
 
• The verb phrase **"has written"** becomes** "has been written by"** in the passive voice to indicate that the action was performed by Sunita.
 
• The part of the sentence **"which fascinates everyone"** is correctly maintained as expressing the effect of the story, highlighting the correct transformation without changing the meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Option 1 says,** "A story which has been written by Sunita fascinates every one." This option, while passively constructed, rearranges the focus of the sentence awkwardly, making it slightly less direct in conveying who is fascinated by the story.
 
• **Option 3 states,** "**Every one fascinates the story which is written by Sunita." This** option incorrectly suggests that everyone is doing the action of fascinating the story, which misrepresents the original sentence's meaning.
 
• **Option 4 suggests,** "Story written by Sunita fascinates everyone." Although this option maintains the meaning and is in a passive construction, it lacks the passive voice marker ("has been written by") that clearly indicates the action performed on the subject (the story).

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

Rajesh ordered his driver to do as he was told.

options.text: Rajesh ordered his driver “Do as you are told”.
Rajesh says to his driver “Do as I told you”.
Rajesh said to his driver, “Do as you are told.”
Rajesh says to his driver “Do as you were told”.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** Rajesh said to his driver “Do as you are told”.

Sentence 3 changes ‘he’ to ‘you’ and ‘was’ to ‘are’, on converting from Indirect to Direct speech. The other sentences do not follow the tense conversion and are incorrect therefore.

questions.question: Management is a set of _____ that can keep a complicated system
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: processes

‘Processes’ means a series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular goal. It is an appropriate fit as management is done in order to achieve set goals and it requires processes for that.

questions.question: of people and technology running _____.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: smoothly 

Running smoothly means something that happens without any problems. The sentence conveys that management is a set of processes that keeps a complicated system running without issues. The other words do not fit properly in the sentence as they do not convey the proper meaning.

questions.question: The most _____ aspects of management include planning budgeting, organizing, staffing, controlling and problem solving.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** important 

‘Important’ means of great significance or value. The word is an appropriate fit as the sentence talks about the most significant aspects of management, and not the difficult or terrible ones.
